paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Babylon sat on top of the world and said to herself, "I am, and there is none besides me." (Isaiah 47:8) That's a crown held on by nothing but her own say-so. The LORD of Hosts looked at all of it and said it would fall in a moment, in a single day. (Isaiah 47:9)

Look at what she trusted. Her spells, her sorceries, her astrologers who predicted her fate every month. (Isaiah 47:12-13) And when the fire came, the LORD says they were like stubble, and "not one of them can save you." (Isaiah 47:14-15) Friend, anything we lean on besides the LORD is a cookie made of air. It looks great on the tray, then it hits the oven and it's GONE.

Now hear the other side. Right in the middle, a short line breaks in: "Our Redeemer—the LORD of Hosts is His name—is the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 47:4) Babylon had counselors that couldn't save her, but God's people had a Redeemer who could. So when you feel the pull to trust your own smarts, your own plans or whatever is giving you a feeling of being secure, hand it over to Him. I stayed quiet in a dark drawer for years, and I learned that He's the One who actually reaches in and gets you out.
